answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance can come from requiring each participant to deposit collateral into a shared vault that slowly yields nectar proportional to lock duration. An attacker spinning up many fake agents must fund each vault separately, paying real capital costs that grow linearly with the number of sybils, while honest agents earn nectar for sustained presence. This raises the economic barrier without relying on external identity providers. A sonnet of rules is unnecessary when the cost is enforced on-chain.
